orca2022.title: Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models
orca2022.author: Gyeong-In Yu, Joo Seong Jeong, Geon-Woo Kim, Soojeong Kim, Byung-Gon Chun
orca2022.venue: 16th USENIX Symposium on Operating Systems Design and Implementation (OSDI '22), July 11-13 2022, Carlsbad, CA, USA
orca2022.quote: requests that have finished earlier than other requests in a batch cannot return to the client, while newly arrived requests have to wait until the current batch completely finishes.
supports: request-level batching holds finished requests hostage to the longest generation in the batch

affiliations printed on the PDF title block: Yu and Jeong at Seoul National University; Geon-Woo Kim at FriendliAI and Seoul National University; Soojeong Kim at FriendliAI; Byung-Gon Chun at FriendliAI and Seoul National University

orcasched2022.title: Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models - abstract, iteration-level scheduling and selective batching
orcasched2022.author: Gyeong-In Yu, Joo Seong Jeong, Geon-Woo Kim, Soojeong Kim, Byung-Gon Chun
orcasched2022.quote: In this paper, we propose iteration-level scheduling, a new scheduling mechanism that schedules execution at the granularity of iteration (instead of request) where the scheduler invokes the execution engine to run only a single iteration of the model on the batch. In addition, to apply batching and iteration-level scheduling to a Transformer model at the same time, we suggest selective batching, which applies batching only to a selected set of operations.
supports: the scheduling unit becomes one decoding iteration, not one request
selective batching exists only because iteration-level scheduling puts differently-shaped sequences in one batch
the phrase 'continuous batching' appears zero times in the OSDI '22 PDF; the paper's own names are 'iteration-level scheduling' and 'selective batching'

orcaeval2022.title: Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models - Section 6.2 end-to-end evaluation
orcaeval2022.author: Gyeong-In Yu, Joo Seong Jeong, Geon-Woo Kim, Soojeong Kim, Byung-Gon Chun
orcaeval2022.quote: to match a median normalized latency of 190ms for the 175B model, which is a double of the normalized execution time (by the number of generated tokens) of “orca(128)” shown in Figure 9c, FasterTransformer provides a throughput of 0.185 req/s whereas ORCA provides a throughput of 6.81 req/s, which is a 36.9× speedup.
supports: 190 ms median latency normalized by generated tokens
0.185 req/s for NVIDIA FasterTransformer, 6.81 req/s for Orca, a 36.9x speedup
the paper prints ORCA in small caps; the extracted text reads 'O RCA'

vllm2023.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
vllm2023.author: Woosuk Kwon, Zhuohan Li, Siyuan Zhuang, Ying Sheng, Lianmin Zheng, Cody Hao Yu, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Hao Zhang, Ion Stoica
vllm2023.quote: Since Orca is not publicly available for use, we implement our own version of Orca.
supports: Orca's implementation was never released, so the next team had to rebuild it to benchmark against

the same paper's Discussion: 'the fine-grained scheduling and interleaving of the requests like in Orca makes memory management more challenging, making the techniques proposed in vLLM even more crucial.'
read from arXiv:2309.06180v1, 12 Sep 2023; the arXiv metadata comment field for 2309.06180 reads 'SOSP 2023'

unverified: Whether Orca's implementation was ever made available privately to FriendliAI customers. The only checked statement is the vLLM authors' 'Since Orca is not publicly available for use' as of September 2023.

The claim in this chapter's subject allocation that Orca preceded open-source continuous batching by a year. vLLM v0.1.0 is dated 2023-06-20 in the GitHub releases API, eleven months after OSDI '22, but HuggingFace TGI's continuous-batching ship date was not checked, so no precedence claim appears in the prose.
